problem:
Find the general solution to the equation 

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-3t{y}^{′}-5y=8{t}^{2},\,t>0.
$$
worked_solution:
First, we need to find the complimentary function ${y}_{c}(t)$ which is the solution to the homogeneous equation

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-3t{y}^{′}-5y=0.
$$

Let $y={t}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {t}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}-3t\cdot \lambda {t}^{\lambda -1}-5{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda }-3\lambda {t}^{\lambda }-5{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {t}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)-3\lambda -5] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)-3\lambda -5 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda -5 & =0 \\ (\lambda -5)(\lambda +1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the roots are $\lambda =-1$ and $\lambda =5.$ Thus, the complimentary function ${y}_{c}(t)$ is

$$
{y}_{c}(t)=\frac{{c}_{1}}{t}+{c}_{2}{t}^{5}.
$$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is proportional to ${t}^{2}.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is of the form 

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=\alpha {t}^{2}
$$

where $\alpha $ is the constant that is to be determined. 

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}t}=2\alpha t,\,\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}{t}^{2}}=2\alpha .
$$

To find the value of $\alpha ,$ we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation and group the terms on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}(2\alpha )-3t(2\alpha t)-5(\alpha {t}^{2}) & =8{t}^{2} \\ (2\alpha -6\alpha -5\alpha ){t}^{2} & =8{t}^{2} \\ -9\alpha {t}^{2} & =8{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get $\alpha =-\frac{8}{9}.$

Hence, the particular integral ${y}_{p}(t)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=-\frac{8{t}^{2}}{9}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(t) & ={y}_{c}(t)+{y}_{p}(t) \\  & =\frac{{c}_{1}}{t}+{c}_{2}{t}^{5}-\frac{8{t}^{2}}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
